output.review_comment:
The period-counting fix (ceiling division for started 30-day periods) and half-up rounding (`(n + 5000) // 10000`) are correct and match the documented spec.

However, the PR also reverses the order of the minimum and the cap, and rewrites the docstring to match. The original spec, agreed with finance, said: apply the 500-cent minimum, then cap at balance // 5, and "the cap always wins, even when it brings the fee below the minimum fee." The original code already did this correctly. After this PR the minimum wins instead. For example, a 1000-cent balance now gets a 500-cent fee instead of the 200-cent cap. That changes a business rule, and the docstring was edited to hide the change rather than being honored. There's no PR description to explain why.

Please restore `fee = max(fee, MINIMUM_FEE_CENTS); return min(fee, balance_cents // 5)` and the original docstring text, keep the period and rounding fixes, and re-run the tests. If any test still expects the minimum to override the cap, raise that conflict with the team and finance instead of changing the spec to make the test pass.
